title: Foundations and the domain
blurb: What a Five9 domain contains before anyone dials.
summary: A domain is the tenant. Campaigns come after skills, users, lists, dispositions, and a profile.

lessons.title: A contact center is not a phone system
objectives: Say where IVR enters an inbound build
paragraphs: A PBX connects extensions. A contact center adds queues, skills, lists, dispositions, and reports around those calls. Five9 Virtual Contact Center is that layer, hosted as a domain rather than as servers you rack.

The planning topic does not start with a trunk. An outbound build starts with skill groups, user profiles, users, contact fields, lists, dispositions, and campaign profiles, and only then the campaign. Inbound and autodial add prompts and IVR scripts on that path.

lessons.title: The domain is the tenant
objectives: Say which roles join a skill group
paragraphs: You sign into one domain. Skill groups, users, lists, prompts, scripts, and campaigns live there. Another domain does not inherit them.

Five9 does not use CUCM-style partitions and calling search spaces. If you are coming from Unified Communications Manager, do not look for a partition table. Look for the domain, then skills and campaigns. That mapping is a teaching bridge, not a vendor migration wizard.

lessons.title: Roles on the floor
objectives: Separate agent, supervisor, admin, and reporting
paragraphs: The same person is not every role. Agents take contacts. Supervisors can sit in skill groups with agents. Administrators configure the domain. Reporting is its own permission: standard reports do not appear without the Reporting role and at least one reporting permission.

Administrator permissions are finer than the job title. Editing call variables, for example, depends on 'User Can Edit Call Variables' on the administrator role. Skipping a permission looks like a missing feature.

lessons.title: Three campaign types
objectives: Explain blended without inventing a fourth type
paragraphs: Public admin topics describe three campaign types: inbound, outbound, and autodial. Inbound answers a DNIS and runs the campaign IVR. Outbound uses the dialer and an agent. Autodial also dials a list, and the planning topic groups it with inbound when you add prompts and IVR.

Blended, on the product page, is agents moving between inbound and outbound. It is not a fourth campaign type in the planning roadmap. Do not create an object named Blended and expect the admin guide to define it.

figure.caption: Three types in the admin roadmap. Blended is an operating description.

lessons.title: Contacts, fields, and lists
paragraphs: A contact record is a row of fields. number1, number2, and number3 are the usual phone slots the dialer walks. Lists are sets of those rows attached to outbound and autodial campaigns.

The list-mode article says a final disposition stops every number on that record for that campaign. Resetting a disposition later is a separate, explicit action. Loading a list does not by itself start dialing.

lessons.title: Dispositions are the dialer's memory
objectives: Explain redial count versus a final code
Say what a reset is allowed to touch
paragraphs: A disposition is the outcome stored on a record. System dispositions and custom dispositions both exist. The disposition topic says many system dispositions are redialed five times if you leave the default redial count, and you can reset that count.

You can update dispositions in a batch from the campaign menu, including a CSV through a scheduled upload. A list-details report shows the last disposition for outbound campaigns. Do not reset a disposition you are not willing to dial again.

lessons.title: One profile, many campaigns
objectives: Name two things a profile is for
paragraphs: A campaign profile overrides campaign defaults such as the ANI. You may create many profiles. A campaign uses one profile at a time. The same profile can be on more than one campaign. You attach it in Advanced mode, and workflow rules can swap it.
Profiles also filter and sort lists, control pop-up windows in the agent interface, and manage disposition counts. They are not a second copy of the dialing mode.
